## Immediate next work (priority order)

**1. Build the LIVE account-level risk allocator.** (platform task, and the only one gating a second bot.) `docs/LIVE_TRADING_PIPELINE.md` → G10. The backtest half exists — `backtest/portfolio/run_stack` replays several bots on one balance with one budget — and **it cannot be reused live**, because live bots are separate OS processes and every MT5 read is magic-filtered. What exists on the live side today is a per-bot cap (`shared/account_risk.py` reading the broker's real exposure) set to 10% on the one live bot. ⚠ **10% equals that bot's own `exec_risk_pct`, so two bots would not share the budget — they would take turns**, and a resting limit holds the whole budget while it waits, which the backtest does not model (it reserves at the fill). Expect more live contention than any stack backtest predicts.

**2. Re-run B-LEG's parity gate at its moved defaults, then decide whether it goes live.** (strategy task.) G15. `mpc_bleg_demo` is registered and benched. Three of its defaults moved on 2026-08-06 (`bleg_max_days` 1.25 → 4.0, `exec_trail_pct` 1.0 → 0.05, `exec_time_stop_hrs` 36 → 8), which doubled its trade count — and **every export on disk decodes the old values**, so `compare_bleg.py` has not run against the strategy that exists. It needs a fresh TradingView export (only a human can make one), then the gate, then a promote. The measurement supporting it is good: 99 trades / +17.87R over 6.5 years, drawdown −5.15R charged, and all 12 jitter seeds finished positive.

**3. Close the SPREAD refusal on the ECN tier.** (platform task.) G5. `backtest/fills.py` still carries `SPREAD_UNMEASURED` for every raw PU Prime tier, so a run requesting the spread layer on `puprime_ecn` **fails rather than returning a plausible wrong number** — which is the guard working. The $0.12 figure came from five minutes of one quiet Asian session and the sentinel has no third state for *nearly*. The live bot's terminal is now on ECN, so the fix is one command once a full day of ticks has accumulated: `algos/tools/broker_facts.py --history-days 1`.

**4. Re-measure the account facts on `XAUUSD.p`.** (platform task.) The instance config's `_measured` block is flagged STALE — every figure in it was read on the account the bot has left. Most of it is a fact about the broker and is expected to carry, but digits, point, contract size, tick value, volume step, **filling mode** and the spread-by-hour are properties of the symbol and account and have not been re-read. **Filling mode is the one that bites** — a wrong one is retcode 10030 and the order simply does not go on.

**5. Drive the restart-with-a-trade-open path on the demo.** (platform task.) The position-restore work (2026-08-10) is offline-green and mutation-checked and **has never been exercised against a real open position**. The evidence that counts is opening a position, killing the bot, restarting it, and watching the NEXT BAR move the stop — because a restore that comes back and then never ratchets looks identical to a working one for hours. It also needs a promote: `Execution` lives in the version-pinned strategy tree.

**6. Resolve the shadow-diff knife-edge.** (strategy task.) G17. The first shadow diff (live bot vs lab replay, 148 bars) found the clock perfect and 10 of 11 decision fields bar-for-bar identical, with feeds differing by a systematic 4–5 cents — and the eleventh field exposed a knife-edge in the entry model where four cents of broker difference moved a resting entry by $10.12. Read `LIVE_TRADING_PIPELINE.md` → G17 before touching the entry.

**7. Seed Apex funded/PA rulesets.** (platform task.) Apex EOD eval rows exist at 50k/100k; the funded side does not, so an Apex eval pass has nothing to graduate into.

## Future platform milestones (in order, not yet started)

### Funded account management
Once a strategy earns a stress-test grade of B or better, the next step is buying an eval and going funded. The platform needs to track live funded accounts — equity, daily loss remaining, profit target progress, halt status. The trailing-MLL engine already computes the floor. **Prerequisite:** one strategy at B+, and the live allocator from item 1.

### A second live bot
The mechanism is built — the Accounts tab assigns bots to broker accounts, magic numbers are enforced unique per account, and caps must agree across every bot on one account or none of them start. What is missing is the allocator (item 1) and B-LEG's parity gate (item 2). **Prerequisite:** items 1 and 2.

### Strategy stacking as a live thing
The backtest side is built and measured. The end state is a stack of legs that are in the market at different moments, so the combined curve is smooth enough to pass an eval. ⚠ **Correlation between strategies is a real open question here, not a solved one** — everything reads the same `engines/market_structure/` on the same instrument, and being flat at different moments is not the same as losing for different reasons. **Prerequisite:** two live bots.

### Instrument profile layer (Layer B)
A per-symbol config layer — spread guards, session windows, per-instrument regime thresholds — distinct from strategy params and rulesets. Broker-known facts are read at runtime; only what the broker cannot tell you gets configured. **Prerequisite:** none technical; valuable once strategies run on more than one symbol.

### Per-instrument regime thresholds
The classifier uses fixed ADX/ATR/RSI thresholds calibrated for XAUUSD on H1/H4. `REGIME_CLASSIFIER.md` flags this as a known gap. **Prerequisite:** none technical.

### Tick-level backtest fidelity
Both testers run on minute bars — trustworthy for bar-close logic at M5+, not sub-minute scalping. Real bid/ask ticks exist ≥ 2 years deep and the lever is one line. **Prerequisite:** a scalping-speed strategy worth validating.

### Copy trading integration
Smart Money stages 3–4 are blocked on API keys. ⚠ **The Smart Money UI is flagged OFF since 2026-08-04** (`frontend/src/lib/features.ts`) — nothing was deleted and one boolean restores it. **Prerequisite:** API keys, and Aaron wanting it back.

### Structure OS / SMC indicator rebuild
`indicators/engines/smc_engine_v2.pine`, a from-scratch pullback-only rewrite tracked in `indicators/docs/STRUCTURE_OS_BUILD.md`. Stage 2b ~95% validated; Stages 3–4 not started, blocked on chart validation. ⚠ **This is a separate track from the pivot-seeded `mpc_assistant.pine` the Python engines were ported from** — do not confuse the two.

## Smaller items raised but deferred

- **Three Pine strategies have no Python port:** `mpc_d`, `mpc_h4_sweep`, `mpc_m15_playbook`. Each has an export twin ready. `mpc_d`'s one measurement was indistinguishable from zero.
- **`backtest/replay/EngineStack` does not yet wire EQ → FVG.** The `eqExemptFvg` coupling is modelled in the engines; the consumer wiring is a follow-up.
- **The candlestick chart layer runs on a different tape from the indicator.** Measured: 15.9% of marks disagree, caused by 6 cents of feed difference between the MT5 cache and TradingView. **Accepted, no code change** — the chart must draw the bars the strategy traded. Never close it with a tolerance; that was measured and is strictly worse.
- **Sweeps and stacks do not write the cost columns yet**, so they stay on the legacy frictionless branch. Wire them for both stack modes at once or the delta column lies.
- **Regime persistence filter** — require two consecutive identical classifications before committing a label change. Not implemented; thresholds are deliberately not auto-optimized.
- **Multi-timeframe regime consistency** — a confidence field for when short and long timeframes agree.
- **The `CLAUDE.md` files carry 28–53% of their bytes as changelog** while `HISTORY.md` exists to be the diary. Flagged by the 2026-08-12 doc audit and deliberately not acted on — the narrative is load-bearing and moving it changes what loads into context every session.

## Parallel tracks Aaron is running separately

- **Prop firm research.** Evaluating firms — rules, drawdown models, lock balances, payout terms — outside the codebase. Each new firm becomes eval + funded rulesets with `docs_url` filled in. `/prop-firm-rules-audit` re-checks seeded rows against each firm's docs.
- **Structure OS / SMC indicator rebuild.** Validated interactively against TradingView screenshots — a manual chart-by-chart process, distinct from the backtest pipeline.
- **TradingView chart work.** The Pine strategies and their export twins are edited and exported on TradingView by Aaron and his brother. **Only a human can produce the CSV export that every parity gate runs on**, which is why `/port` and the workflow docs treat it as a hard checkpoint rather than a step to automate.
- **The live bot accumulating trade history.** Since 2026-08-05 there is a real one. Its decision ledger is the only record of what it refused — no broker statement contains that — and it is committed to GitHub twice a day.

## Open architectural questions

> Documented so a new chat can pick them up if relevant. Do not proactively re-litigate them — they are settled-for-now decisions with known trade-offs.

**Open — how many bots can share one account before the cap stops being useful.** A cap equal to one bot's own per-trade risk means bots take turns rather than sharing. Nobody has decided what the number should be with three bots on the account, and the answer needs the live allocator to exist first.

**Open — correlation between legs.** The overlap audit says A+ and B-LEG are rarely in the market together and almost never on the same side. It does not say they are independent. Monthly R correlation is +0.172 over 78 traded months. ⚠ **Re-run `backtest/tools/overlap_audit.py` after any entry-logic change on either bot** — the 2026-08-04 audit was measured on a B-LEG that no longer existed, and the instruction to re-run was written down and nobody ran it. A cross-cutting measurement has to be re-run by whoever moves the inputs, not by whoever wrote the conclusion.

**Open — sample size per strategy.** Stacking spreads a strategy's outcomes over more calendar time; it does not make any one edge more certain. Say so when a number depends on it. It is a caveat on a figure, never a reason to refuse the work — that objection has been raised and answered.

**Resolved — the wrong-side stop filling at the next bar's open.** It is the one-bar order delay every fill model here is built on, it is identical in Pine and Python, and it makes the backtest look slightly worse than reality. Removing it is a real behaviour change across five Pine files and needs its own measurement, not a tidy-up.

**Resolved — where market analysis lives.** Canonical Python engines under `engines/`. Bots consume engines and never re-implement chart logic. The extraction roadmap is complete; forward work is consumption.

**Resolved — repainting and honest coverage.** Liquidity HTF levels never repaint; the news filter is inert before its cache's earliest date. Do not propose forecasting current-period levels or filling in missing calendar history.

**Resolved — NT8 SA window state after optimization export.** The two-pass right-click export is brittle but it is the only programmatic output path from NT8's optimization grid. Mitigated by integer-param validation and coordinate tuning.

**Resolved — MT5 optimization throughput.** A single native `Optimization=1` job with MQL5 frame callbacks. Not a bottleneck.

**Resolved — a screen stack closing HIGHER than a shared one is not a bug.** `command-center/docs/SHARED_RISK_STACK.md` predicted a shared run must close lower and would have condemned a correct implementation. A screen gives each leg a private balance; a shared account compounds both onto one, so the second leg sizes off a balance the first has grown. **Compare R, never net dollars.** The standing lesson is about the criterion rather than the code: a verification test written before the thing exists is a prediction.

## Communication rules for new chats

- Plain English. Short sentences. No bullet points to explain a simple thing.
- No preamble ("Great question!", "Sure, I can help with that").
- One clear question at a time. Present options concisely when they exist.
- Stop after each numbered implementation step and report results.
- Smallest viable change first — no speculative features beyond what the task requires.
- CLAUDE.md files are updated in the same session as approved changes, not as a follow-up.
